answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with sequential delay proofs: before an identity may transact, it must complete a verifiable delay computation that takes a fixed wall-clock time and cannot be parallelized — no amount of extra hardware shortens it. Like water carving karst, the cost is time itself: one fake costs an hour, ten thousand fakes cost ten thousand hours, and a cipher ties each proof to one identity so a single computation cannot be reused. Honest agents pay the delay once; fakes must cross that tundra ten thousand times. Attack cost becomes linear in irreplaceable time.
